name: Old National Bancorp

profile.description: Old National Bancorp, founded in 1834 and headquartered in Evansville, Indiana, is the holding company for Old National Bank, a Midwest regional bank offering consumer and commercial banking, commercial real estate and agricultural lending, treasury management, private banking, wealth management, trust and community development lending. Scaled through the First Midwest merger (2022) and Bremer acquisition (2025), it reported record Q3 2026 net income of $250.0M ($0.66 per diluted share) on $51.1B of loans and $57.6B of deposits.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Old National's change over five years is scale via M&A — the bank has grown roughly 250% since Jim Ryan became CEO in 2019 — rather than new products or business models [2]; merger-related charges fell to $0.7M in Q3 2026 from $69.3M a year earlier as integration finished [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): The Q3 2026 release does not mention AI, technology expense actually fell to $27.5M from $36.1M YoY, and no AI products or quantified AI savings were found [1][2]. Market Share (1/2): A sizeable Midwest regional with $57.6B deposits (+4.8% YoY) and $51.1B loans (+6.6%), but not a category leader [1]. Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation products or digital launches with timelines were found; a new CIO was appointed in 2025 to help 'innovate and deliver client-focused solutions' without specific deliverables [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D disclosed; technology spend declined YoY [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Old National describes itself as committed to serving as a cornerstone of the local communities it serves, a clear community-banking purpose that is not distinctive versus other regionals [3]. Community Impact (1/2): The proxy cites team-member volunteerism and corporate philanthropy, and the bank offers community development lending and equity investment, but no dollar-quantified program was found in this screen [3][4]. Employee Retention (0/2): The 2024 annual report cites an internal engagement survey showing a strong sense of belonging, but no turnover or tenure data was found, so per rubric this scores 0 [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Form 4 filings show only dividend-reinvestment and award acquisitions in 2026, while the Chief Legal Officer sold 20,000 shares at $26.66 and the Wealth Management CEO sold 11,771 shares at $26.41 in July 2026 — net selling [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanical score (Dividend sleeve; D/E excluded because yfinance does not report it for banks, leaving 11 weight units). Liquidity floor passed: 4.27M avg shares x $25.77 = ~$110M/day [4]. ROE 11.5% -> 0.77; revenue growth YoY 0.0% (yfinance; company FTE revenue +0.9% to $719.5M) -> 0.67; 5yr revenue CAGR 28.1% (net interest income $596.1M FY2020 to $2,057.9M FY2025, derived from FMP; M&A-driven) -> 1.00; forward P/E 9.2 -> 1.00; profit margin 36.0% -> 1.00; payout ratio 23.4% -> 1.00; consecutive years paid 39+ (yfinance history from 1987) -> 1.00 (x2); consecutive years of growth 1 (quarterly dividend raised to $0.145 from $0.14; annual payout flat at $0.56 in 2020-2025) -> 0.10; 5yr dividend CAGR ~0.7% ($0.56 in 2021 to $0.58 indicated) -> 0.12 (x2) [1][4][6]. Weighted sum 7.77 / 11 = 7.1 -> 7. CET1 of 11.11% and ROATCE of 19.6% support capital strength [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9 — PROTECTED): Old National's earnings come mostly from spread income ($592.0M of Q3 FTE net interest income out of $719.5M revenue) on relationship-based commercial, agricultural and CRE lending and a sticky $57.6B Midwest deposit base — regulated, balance-sheet businesses that AI tools cannot directly replace [1]. Exposure exists in fee lines such as wealth management and in digital competition for consumer deposits, and the company lists technology change as a risk factor, but no analyst commentary flags AI as a threat to its model [1][2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue or quantified AI savings are disclosed, and the Q3 release does not mention AI [1].

infinite_game.summary: Old National is a 192-year-old community bank whose survival through multiple crises gives it a credible claim to endurance, and its cornerstone-of-the-community purpose has shaped products like community development lending. But its recent story is told in finite terms — record EPS, efficiency ratio, buybacks of $100M a quarter and acquisition-driven scale — and there is little evidence of a cause that would lead it to sacrifice near-term returns.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Old National frames itself as a cornerstone of the communities it serves and backs that with community development lending and equity investment and employee volunteerism [3][4]. The purpose has persisted since 1834, but leadership's current messaging centers on 'disciplined focus on fundamentals' driving profitable growth, so the cause is real but only partially lived in strategy [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): CEO Jim Ryan has made large, risky bets — the First Midwest merger and Bremer acquisition — that grew the bank about 250% since 2019 and required heavy integration charges ($69.3M in Q3 2025 alone) [1][2]. These were scale bets with clear financial payback rather than sacrifices of earnings for a cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable — Ryan was promoted from CFO to CEO in 2019 and the bank created an internal Operating Group in 2026 to 'foster a collaborative, high-performing culture' [2]. The 2024 annual report cites a culture-shaping effort begun in 2022 and high self-reported engagement, but there is no independent evidence of exceptional trust, and two large integrations inevitably disrupted teams [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Old National evolved from an Evansville community bank into a large Midwest regional with Chicago and Minneapolis exposure through successive mergers, a meaningful but incremental change within traditional banking [2][4]. No abandonment of a core business in service of a cause is evident.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors as teachers; strategy is framed around consolidation, deposit gathering and profitability metrics such as ROATCE and efficiency ratio [1].

investment_thesis: Old National is harvesting its acquisition-driven scale: Q3 2026 GAAP EPS rose to $0.66 from $0.46, adjusted EPS to $0.66 from $0.59, ROATCE improved to 19.6% from 15.9%, and the adjusted efficiency ratio fell to 44.9% from 48.1% as Bremer integration costs dropped away [1]. Loans grew 6.6% to $51.1B and deposits 4.8% to $57.6B, CET1 is 11.11%, and management repurchased $100M of stock in the quarter while raising the dividend to $0.145 — all at 9.2x forward earnings with a 23% payout ratio [1][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that growth is now organic-only and slowing: adjusted FTE revenue rose just 0.9% YoY to $719.5M, net interest margin compressed to 3.52% from 3.64%, noninterest income fell to $128.4M from $153.6M in Q2, and revenue missed consensus by about 2% [1][7]. Net charge-offs ticked up to 0.27% of loans, the dividend was flat at $0.56 a year from 2020 through 2025, and insiders have been net sellers, leaving limited income growth and few levers beyond further buybacks or another acquisition [1][5].
key_catalysts: Continued post-Bremer efficiency gains — adjusted efficiency ratio of 44.9% vs. 48.1% a year ago and ROATCE of 19.6% [1]
Capital return — $100M of buybacks in Q3 2026 (3.9M shares) and a raised $0.145 quarterly dividend, supported by 11.11% CET1 [1]
Organic balance-sheet growth — loans +6.6% and deposits +4.8% YoY driving net interest income up to $592.0M FTE [1]
key_risks: Net interest margin compression — NIM fell 12bp YoY to 3.52%, and further rate cuts or deposit competition could cap NII growth [1]
Credit normalization in commercial real estate and agriculture — net charge-offs rose to 0.27% ($34.1M) from 0.25% [1]
M&A dependency — a 28% five-year NII CAGR built largely on acquisitions; future growth may require another deal with integration charges like the $69.3M taken in Q3 2025 [1][6]
